text: dsh-work-crew 是面向 DSH 网页与桌面客户端的多模型协作插件：它注册任务管理工具，并在 composer dock 提供协作看板。可初始化项目任务板、声明任务依赖和读写产物锁，再把任务简报发送给本机 AI 应用并收集结果；看板显示任务、成员、锁和时间线。适合希望让多个本机 AI 应用分工完成编码与评审的用户；需要配置受支持的本机应用和工作区。

dsh-work-crew coordinates local AI apps in DSH with task tools and a composer board. Set dependencies and artifact locks, dispatch briefs, and collect results. The board tracks workers and progress; configure supported local apps and project workspaces.
我想让几个本机 AI 应用分工写代码和互相评审，并能追踪任务进度。
DSH 能不能把有依赖关系的任务派给不同助手，同时避免它们同时改同一份文件？
I want to coordinate local AI apps on coding tasks, track their progress, and prevent conflicting edits.
dsh-work-crew 的功能「任务板与协作派单」：通过 team_init 初始化项目，再用任务工具声明负责人、依赖与读写锁，并派发简报给本机 AI 应用；任务板展示状态和时间线。
dsh-work-crew 的功能「项目知识库」：可搜索内置或项目自定义的参考条目，并按任务标签、内容关键词和负责人挑选条目，随任务简报提供给执行者。
dsh-work-crew 会把任务简报通过调试协议输入到用户选择的本机 AI 应用；简报内容可能由该应用连接的服务处理，具体服务取决于用户的应用与账号配置。
dsh-work-crew 的维护与更新元数据：活跃维护；距最后推送 15 天；提交数 13；更新频次 unknown；近 90 天提交 未知；开放 Issue 未知；仓库健康分 62/100（置信度 low）。

一个指令。一支有纪律的本机 AI 班组。

简体中文 · English

--- `dsh-work-crew` is a [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that turns the AI apps already installed on your machine — Doubao, WorkBuddy, ZCode, Qoder — into a **crew with a task board**.

dsh-work-crew README · dsh-work-crew：DSH stays the orchestrator. It does not write your code itself; it plans, dispatches, enforces locks,
collects receipts and keeps the books. The crew does the typing.
dsh-work-crew README · Why：One model reviewing its own work is the weakest link in every AI coding session:

dsh-work-crew README · Why：| Failure | What the crew does instead |
|---|---|
| **Self-review blind spot** — the model checks its own output | A different model reviews it; the implementer never signs off on itself |
| **Concurrent edits** — writing and reviewing the same file at once | Artifact locks: `write:landing:hero` and `read:landing` cannot overlap in time |
| **Lost progress** — who is waiting for whom, asked again next session | A task board on disk (`.dsh-team/`) with dependencies, locks and timeline |
dsh-work-crew README · Install：```powershell
dsh-work-crew README · from GitHub：dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:yxyusage/dsh-work-crew

dsh-work-crew README · from a local checkout：dsh plugin --profile desktop add "E:\path\to\dsh-work-crew"
```

Then fully quit DSH (tray → Quit) and reopen it.

dsh-work-crew README · Quick start：```text
team_init          → create .dsh-team/ (mission, roles, board, outbox)
team_add_task      → title, worker, dependsOn, write/read locks, expect
team_dispatch      → builds a brief, enforces locks, sends it (queues when busy)
team_collect       → wait for receipts; takes taskIds, returns whoever finishes first

A typical plan:

dsh-work-crew README · Quick start：```
T1  implement hero      WorkBuddy   write:landing:hero
T2  review landing      Doubao      read:landing        ← waits for T1 (write×read)
T3  product discussion  Doubao      —                   ← runs in parallel with T1
T4  docs                Qoder       write:docs          dependsOn: [T1, T2]

dsh-work-crew README · Tools：| Tool | When to use |
|---|---|
| `team_init` | first time in a project; records reference dirs and required docs |
| `team_status` | who runs what, queue depth, last activity, held locks |
| `team_add_task` | declare worker, dependencies, locks, deadline, expected artifacts |
| `team_dispatch` | send a brief; **takes `taskIds` to dispatch several in one step**; queues when a worker is busy |
| `team_collect` | wait for receipts: `taskIds` returns whoever finishes first |
| `team_reassign` | move a task to another worker, keeping brief and history |
| `team_reopen` | a false completion → back to running, without re-sending |
| `team_resubmit` | artifacts now exist → re-check expect instead of re-dispatching |
| `team_release` | close a task (refuses `done` while expected artifacts are missing) |
| `team_split_html` | split a single-file page into html/css/js so three workers can edit in parallel |
| `team_shot` | screenshot to a file, path only — device emulation for mobile widths |
| `team_workers` | status / preflight / restart / ping |

dsh-work-crew README · Workers：| id | App | Good at | Debug port |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workbuddy` | WorkBuddy | implementing, running commands, verifying builds | 9332 |
| `doubao` | Doubao | visual review, ideas, reading screenshots | 9331 |
| `zcode` | ZCode | implementation / second opinion (limited free quota) | 9334 |
| `qoder` | Qoder | implementation / read-only audits (VS Code family) | 9335 |

dsh-work-crew README · How it works：- **Driven over CDP.** The plugin launches each app with `--remote-debugging-port` and types into its chat box.
  Windows can stay offscreen; nothing steals your mouse.
- **Completion is a hard signal.** WorkBuddy's "已完成" badge; Doubao/ZCode/Qoder's `@@END@@` sentinel.
  No guessing from text stillness.
- **File handoff.** Workers write reports to `.dsh-team/outbox/<id>.md` and reply with one line.
  The body never enters the orchestrator's context — that is where the token savings come from.
- **Locks with hierarchy.** `landing` covers `landing:hero`; siblings (`hero`, `meta`) run in parallel.
- **Queue, not stuck.** A busy worker queues the task (`queued`, no locks, no timeout) and promotes it when the
  current one is collected.
- **Budget.** `deadlineMin` (default 45) flags a stalled task; at twice the budget it is blocked and its locks released.
- **Artifacts are checked.** `expect` paths must exist before a task counts as done; the outbox file is added automatically.

dsh-work-crew README · Screenshots: two traps that produce false reviews：Use `team_shot` — it already avoids both traps and returns only a path:

```text
team_shot { "target": "index.html", "out": "shots/mobile-390.png", "width": 390, "mobile": true }
```

**Trap 1 — capturing mid-animation.** A headless shot without a virtual clock lands on the fade-in, so the page looks
half-transparent. `team_shot` emulates `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` and waits for the layout to settle.
section: Screenshots: two traps that produce false reviews

dsh-work-crew README · Screenshots: two traps that produce false reviews：**Trap 2 — resizing the window instead of emulating the device.** `--window-size=390,844` sets the *window*, but the
layout keeps the desktop viewport (~980px), so the shot is a cropped desktop page. That reads as "the layout overflows"
and sends a reviewer chasing a bug that does not exist. Device emulation is the only honest mobile shot, and
`team_shot` checks `scrollWidth` for you: if it equals the viewport, the layout is fine.

dsh-work-crew README · Guardrails：| Guard | What it does |
|---|---|
| `review: true` | The reviewer gets **requirement + `git diff` + rubric only**. It is told not to read the implementer's report — a reviewer that inherits the author's narrative inherits the author's blind spots. |
| Snapshot review | The changed files are copied to `.dsh-team/snapshots/<id>/` and the reviewer reads **the copy**, so the review takes no read lock and the next implementation starts immediately. Diffing starts from the implementer's recorded `baseCommit`, so committed work still shows up. |
| `verify: "pnpm build"` | The acceptance command runs in the project before the task may close. A red build blocks the task; no green build, no done. |
| `risk: "high"` | High-risk work (auth, payments, CI, secrets, installers) **never self-approves**: collecting it only reports "awaiting approval" until a human re-collects with `confirm: true`. |
| `rubric.md` + review round counter | `team_init` writes the project's acceptance rubric; every review carries it. From the 4th review of the same artifact, the brief asks whether the *plan* is wrong instead of requesting another patch list. |
| `crossCheck: true` | A

`team_knowledge` ships curated references; the matching ones are injected into the brief automatically — authors do not have to remember to ask.

dsh-work-crew README · Knowledge base：Matching: explicit `tags` on the task win; otherwise keywords in the title and brief decide. **The worker matters too** —
Doubao is held to design/motion, Qoder to security/structure, ZCode to copy/docs, WorkBuddy to implementation. At most 4
entries, each rendered as link + how to use + what not to do + 3 rules.

dsh-work-crew README · Knowledge base：And the loop closes at review time: a review task receives **the checklist the implementer was given**, up to 8 rules,
each to be judged `done / not done (with location) / not applicable`. That turns "check it" into findings you can act on.

Project-specific entries go in `.dsh-team/knowledge/<id>.md` and override built-ins by id:

dsh-work-crew README · Knowledge base：```text
team_knowledge { "action": "add", "id": "brand-guide", "title": "品牌规范", "tags": ["frontend","color"],
  "url": "https://...", "use": "配色只从这 5 个色里选", "avoid": "自创渐变",
  "rules": ["主色 #1f6feb，只用于主按钮", "正文色 #0f1115 / #e6e8eb"] }
```

dsh-work-crew README · Workflow：```mermaid flowchart TB A["team_add_task
tags · locks · expect · verify · risk"] --> B{"能否并行？
不同文件 / 不同 worker"} B -- 是 --> C["team_dispatch taskIds
一次派多个"] B -- 否 --> D["team_dispatch"]

dsh-work-crew README · Workflow：Four gates stand between "the model says done" and done: **artifacts exist** (`expect`), **the build passes** (`verify`),
**the page actually runs** (console errors + overflow + mechanical gates), and **a reviewer judges the same checklist the
implementer was given**. Any failure blocks the task instead of passing it downstream.
dsh-work-crew README · Token economics：Measured on a real run (18 tasks, one landing page). Method: UTF-8 3 bytes per Chinese character, 1 token ≈ 1.5 characters.

dsh-work-crew README · Token economics：| Quantity | Measured | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Worker output kept on disk | **115,188 bytes** in 17 outbox files ≈ 25.6k tokens | With chat delivery this enters the orchestrator's context and is re-sent on **every** later step |
| Briefs sent to workers | 57,864 bytes ≈ 12.9k tokens | Sent over CDP straight into the apps — never touches the orchestrator's context |
| Average single output | 6,776 bytes ≈ 1.5k tokens | One read costs more than the whole dispatch brief |
| Dispatch calls | 8 calls for 18 tasks (`taskIds` batch) | ~10 fewer steps than one call per task |
| Collect calls | 10 calls for 18 tasks (`taskIds` batch) | Whoever finishes first returns; no polling loop |
| Restarts | 1 call for four apps (`restart all`) | Was 4 steps, each re-sending the conversation |
| Screenshots | path only, image never read | Each image read costs ~1–2k tokens and stays in context |

dsh-work-crew README · Token economics：The arithmetic that matters: a step costs *context size × 1*. Keeping 25.6k tokens of worker prose out of the context
saves that amount on every subsequent step. Over a 40-step run that is roughly **a million token-equivalents of context
traffic** that never happens (mostly cache reads — cheap, but not free).

What it costs: each dispatch carries ~800 bytes of references plus a ~2k-token checklist to the worker. That is paid to
the worker's API, not to the orchestrator.

dsh-work-crew README · Requirements：- Windows with DSH Desktop (or DSH Web + Node 22+).
- At least one of the four apps installed and **logged in**.
- In each app: select the project folder as its workspace, and allow auto-approval / full access.
- The plugin launches the apps itself; an app already running without a debug port must be restarted
  (`team_workers {"action":"restart","worker":"doubao"}`), which is also the fix when a port goes stale.

dsh-work-crew README · Limits：- Selectors are tied to each app's UI. App updates can break them; every worker carries a `spec` version and
  `team_workers {"action":"ping"}` tells you whether the chain still works.
- Quota cannot be read from any of the four apps. A worker that runs out mid-task is detected by timeout and
  is meant to be re-dispatched with `team_reassign`.
- One app can hold only one in-flight task. That is a property of a single input channel, not a bug.
- Kimi desktop is not supported: it rejects both `--remote-debugging-port` and `--remote-debugging-pipe`.

dsh-work-crew README · Layout：```
index.js            tools + the /dsh-work-crew/state route for the panel
lib/team.js         board, locks, briefs, roles, queue
lib/cdp.js          CDP sessions, launch, typing, reading, completion rules
client.js           sidebar panel (React, conversation.composer.dock)

一个指令。一支有纪律的本机 AI 班组。
One prompt. A working team.

简体中文 · English

--- `dsh-work-crew` 是 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 的插件：把你电脑上已经装好的 AI 软件——豆包、WorkBuddy、ZCode、Qoder——变成一支**有任务板的班组**。 DSH 只当调度者：拆任务、派单、加锁、收单、记账。代码由班组来写，DSH 不自己动手。

dsh-work-crew README · 为什么需要它：一个模型自己写、自己审，是 AI 编码里最弱的一环：

| 问题 | 班组怎么解 |
|---|---|
| **自评盲区**：模型检查自己的产出 | 换一个模型来评；实现者不验收自己的活 |
| **并发打架**：一边改、一边评同一个文件 | 产物锁：`write:landing:hero` 与 `read:landing` 不可能同时进行 |
| **进度失忆**：谁在等谁，换个会话就断片 | 任务板落盘（`.dsh-team/`）：依赖、锁、时间线都在 |
dsh-work-crew README · 安装：```powershell
dsh-work-crew README · 从 GitHub 安装：dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:yxyusage/dsh-work-crew

dsh-work-crew README · 或从本地目录安装：dsh plugin --profile desktop add "E:\path\to\dsh-work-crew"
```

装完**完全退出 DSH**（托盘 → 退出）再重新打开。

dsh-work-crew README · 快速开始：```text
team_init        → 建 .dsh-team/（mission、roles、board、outbox）
team_add_task    → 标题、负责人、依赖、读写锁、验收产物
team_dispatch    → 生成简报、检查锁、投喂发送（忙时自动排队）
team_collect     → 等回执；可传多个 taskId，谁先完成返回谁

一个典型排班：

```
T1  实现 Hero      WorkBuddy   write:landing:hero
T2  评审落地页     豆包        read:landing         ← 等 T1（写×读互斥）
T3  产品讨论       豆包        —                    ← 与 T1 并行
T4  写文档         Qoder       write:docs           dependsOn: [T1, T2]

dsh-work-crew README · 工具：| 工具 | 什么时候用 |
|---|---|
| `team_init` | 项目第一次用；顺便记下参考目录和必读文档 |
| `team_status` | 谁在跑、队列多长、最后活动、锁被谁占 |
| `team_add_task` | 声明负责人、依赖、锁、超时预算、验收产物 |
| `team_dispatch` | 派单；**传 taskIds 可一次派多个**；worker 忙时自动排队（不占锁、不计超时） |
| `team_collect` | 收单：传 `taskIds`，谁先完成返回谁 |
| `team_reassign` | 改派给另一个 worker，保留简报与时间线 |
| `team_reopen` | 误判完成 → 打回进行中，不重新发送 |
| `team_resubmit` | 产物补齐了 → 只重查 expect，不用重新派单 |
| `team_release` | 收尾；产物不齐时拒绝标 done |
| `team_split_html` | 把单文件 HTML 拆成 html/css/js，让三个 worker 各改一个文件、真正并行 |
| `team_shot` | 截图存盘只回路径；手机宽度用设备模拟，不会拍到"被裁切的桌面版" |
| `team_workers` | status / preflight / restart / ping |

dsh-work-crew README · 四名成员：| id | 软件 | 擅长 | 调试端口 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workbuddy` | WorkBuddy | 写代码、跑命令、验证构建 | 9332 |
| `doubao` | 豆包 | 视觉评审、创意、看截图 | 9331 |
| `zcode` | ZCode | 实现 / 第二意见（免费额度有限） | 9334 |
| `qoder` | Qoder | 实现 / 只读审计（VS Code 系） | 9335 |

dsh-work-crew README · 怎么运作：- **走 CDP 驱动。** 插件带 `--remote-debugging-port` 拉起各家，直接往它的输入框里打字。窗口可以放在屏幕外，不抢鼠标。
- **完成判定是硬信号。** WorkBuddy 看「已完成」徽标；豆包 / ZCode / Qoder 看 `@@END@@` 哨兵。不靠"文字不动了"猜。
- **文件交接。** worker 把报告写进 `.dsh-team/outbox/<id>.md`，聊天里只回一行。正文不进调度者上下文——省 token 就省在这。
- **层级锁。** `landing` 覆盖 `landing:hero`；同级的 `hero` 与 `meta` 可以并行。
- **排队不是卡死。** worker 忙时任务进 `queued`：不占锁、不计超时；当前任务收单后自动顶上。
- **有预算。** `deadlineMin`（默认 45 分钟）到点标停滞，两倍时间自动 blocked 并释放锁。
- **验收产物。** `expect` 里的路径必须真实存在才算完成；`outbox/<id>.md` 会自动加进去。

dsh-work-crew README · 六道闸门：| 闸门 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `review: true` | 评审只拿到 **需求 + `git diff` + 验收标准**，并被明确要求**不要读实现者的报告**。读了实现者的叙述，就会继承他的盲区。 |
| 评审快照 | 改动文件先复制到 `.dsh-team/snapshots/<id>/`，评审读**副本**，因此不占读锁——下一个实现可以立刻开始。diff 从实现任务记录的 `baseCommit` 起算，**已提交的改动也不会漏**。 |
| `verify: "pnpm build"` | 收单前在项目里**真跑一次**验收命令。红了就 blocked——没有绿色构建，就没有 done。 |
| `risk: "high"` | 高风险改动（鉴权/支付/CI/密钥/安装器）**不能自己放行**：收单只回「待确认」，必须人再调一次 `confirm: true`。 |
| `rubric.md` + 评审轮次 | `team_init` 生成项目验收标准，评审任务自动带上；同一产物从第 4 轮评审起，简报会先问「是不是方案本身有问题」，而不是继续要补丁清单。 |
| `crossCheck: true` | 评审出问题后，再派**第二个评审者**逐条投票：成立 / 误报 / 证据不足。只留成立的。 |

dsh-work-crew README · 知识库：「做得好看点」等于没说。「看这个，这么用，这三条满足了才算完」才会有变化。

`team_knowledge` 内置一批参考，派单时**按标签自动匹配**带进简报，不用每次手动点名。

dsh-work-crew README · 知识库：| 条目 | 管什么 | 出处 |
|---|---|---|
| `de-ai-slop` | 紫蓝渐变、三卡片首屏、emoji 当图标、假占位——一律不用 | [反 AI 味清单](https://github.com/infometa/workbuddyskills/blob/main/experts/design-engine/skills/quality-review/references/anti-slop-checklist.md) |
| `frontend-ui` | 组件结构与四态（默认/hover/focus/disabled） | [shadcn AI Elements](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/ai-elements) |

dsh-work-crew README · 知识库：匹配规则：任务上的 `tags` 优先；没写就看标题和简报里的关键词；**还看是谁在做**——豆包被要求对设计和动效负责，Qoder 对安全和结构，ZCode 对文案和文档，WorkBuddy 对实现。最多 4 条。

闭环在评审那一端：评审任务会收到**实现者当初被要求遵守的那份清单**（最多 8 条），逐条判「做到了 / 没做到（指位置）/ 不适用」。这样"看看行不行"就变成了可执行的结论。

项目专属条目放 `.dsh-team/knowledge/<id>.md`，同 id 覆盖内置条目：

```text
team_knowledge { "action": "add", "id": "brand-guide", "title": "品牌规范", "tags": ["frontend","color"],
  "use": "配色只从这 5 个色里选", "avoid": "自创渐变",
  "rules": ["主色 #1f6feb，只用于主按钮", "正文色 #0f1115 / #e6e8eb"] }
```

dsh-work-crew README · 工作流：```mermaid flowchart TB A["team_add_task
tags · 锁 · expect · verify · risk"] --> B{"能否并行？
不同文件 / 不同 worker"} B -- 是 --> C["team_dispatch taskIds
一次派多个"] B -- 否 --> D["team_dispatch"] 从「模型说完成了」到「真的完成」之间有四道闸门：**产物存在**（expect）、**构建通过**（verify）、**页面真的能跑**（控制台 + 溢出 + 机械规则）、**评审按实现者拿到的同一份清单逐条判**。任何一道不过就 blocked，不会往下游传。

dsh-work-crew README · Token 账（实测）：| 项目 | 实测 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| 产出留在磁盘 | 17 个 outbox 共 **115,188 字节** ≈ 2.56 万 token | 若走聊天投递，这些会永久留在调度者上下文，**每步重发一次** |
| 简报发给 worker | 57,864 字节 ≈ 1.29 万 token | 走 CDP 直接进软件，**不进 DSH 上下文** |
| 单份产出平均 | 6,776 字节 ≈ 1.5k token | 读一份的成本比整份简报还高 |
| 派单调用 | 18 个任务用了 8 次（批量 taskIds） | 比逐个派省约 10 步 |
| 收单调用 | 18 个任务用了 10 次（批量 taskIds） | 谁先完成先返回，不轮询 |
| 重启 | 四家一次（restart all） | 原来要 4 步，每步重发一遍对话 |
| 截图 | 只回路径，图片不进上下文 | 每读一张图约 1–2k token，且永久留存 |

dsh-work-crew README · Token 账（实测）：关键算式：**一步的成本 = 上下文大小 × 1**。把 2.56 万 token 的产出挡在上下文外，之后每一步都省这一份；跑 40 步就是约 **100 万 token 当量的上下文流量**没发生（大部分是缓存读，便宜但不是免费）。

代价也要说清：每次派单会多带约 800 字节参考 + 一份约 2k token 的对照清单给 worker——这笔钱花在 worker 的 API 上，不花在 DSH 上。

dsh-work-crew README · 前置条件：- Windows + DSH Desktop（或 DSH Web + Node 22+）。
- 四家里至少装一家并**已登录**。
- 每家软件里：把项目目录选成工作区，权限开"自动审批 / 完全访问"。
- 软件由插件带端口启动；已经在跑但没有调试端口的，用
  `team_workers {"action":"restart","worker":"doubao"}` 重启一次（端口掉了也用它）。

dsh-work-crew README · 已知限制：- 选择器绑定各家 UI，软件大改版可能失效。每个 worker 带 `spec` 版本号，
  `team_workers {"action":"ping"}` 可以一条命令验证整条链路还通不通。
- 四家都读不到剩余额度。额度中途耗尽只能靠超时发现，再用 `team_reassign` 改派。
- 同一个软件同时只能有一个在途任务——这是单输入通道的物理限制，不是 bug。
- Kimi 桌面版不支持：它既拒绝 `--remote-debugging-port` 也拒绝 `--remote-debugging-pipe`。
